stem: Why does WCAG 2.1 require alternative text for meaningful non-text elements such as photographs and informative diagrams?

options.text: Because the alternative text is displayed as a visible caption beneath each image.
options.shortLabel: Alt text shown as a visible caption
options.rationale: Captions are visible text added to the page. Alternative text is exposed to assistive technology and is not displayed as a caption.

options.text: Because alternative text provides a textual description that search engines can use to index visual content.
options.rationale: Alternative text can help search engines understand images, but its accessibility purpose is to provide a text equivalent that can be presented to users who cannot perceive the visual content.

options.text: Because meaningful images must include detailed descriptions that remain visible alongside the original content, regardless of the user's assistive technology.
options.rationale: Visible descriptions can benefit many users, but alternative text does not have to appear visually. It can be programmatically exposed to assistive technologies without being displayed on screen.

options.text: Because alternative text can be converted into speech, braille, or enlarged print.
options.rationale: Text alternatives allow non-text information to be presented through different sensory modalities and formats, including speech, braille, and magnified text. This makes the information accessible to people who cannot perceive the original visual content.

explanation: Text is a flexible medium in information technology. A text alternative lets user agents present the same information as speech, braille, or enlarged text, so the content is available in whichever form the user needs.

references.title: WCAG 2.1 Understanding Docs: Understanding SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content
